labels.swarmItem: LAB 1 — directory /workspace/repo/src/lab1/. Classic 5-stage in-order RV32I pipeline (IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB); branches are resolved in the ID stage and the ID stage contains forwarding muxes. Implement: core/ALU.v (12 ops per its parameters: ADD,SUB,AND,OR,XOR,SLL,SRL,SLT,SLTU,SRA,A+4,B-passthrough, plus zero and signed-overflow flags), core/ImmGen.v (I/B/J/S/U sign-extension), core/RAM_B.v (byte-addressable data memory, byte/half/word access), core/Regs.v (31-entry regfile, write-through, dual read ports, x0 hardwired 0), core/REG_IF_ID.v (stall+flush), core/REG_ID_EX.v (flush-on-hazard), core/REG_EX_MEM.v, core/REG_MEM_WB.v, common/cmp_32.v (6-mode EQ/NE/LT/LTU/GE/GEU comparator), core/CtrlUnit.v (full RV32I control signal generation), core/HazardDetectionUnit.v (forwarding + load-use stall logic), core/RV32core.v (top-level MUX wiring: PC select, forwarding, ALU input muxes). The test program source is all_test.s; rom.mem is preloaded. Verify the CPU runs all_test.s correctly.

LAB 2 — directory /workspace/repo/src/lab2/. Same 5-stage pipeline as lab1, extended with CSR registers and exceptions. Implement every TODO module: core/ALU.v, core/ImmGen.v, core/RAM_B.v, core/Regs.v, core/REG_IF_ID.v, core/REG_ID_EX.v, core/REG_EX_MEM.v, core/REG_MEM_WB.v, common/cmp_32.v, core/CtrlUnit.v, core/HazardDetectionUnit.v, core/RV32core.v, PLUS core/CSRRegs.v (CSR register file supporting CSRRW/CSRRS/CSRRC) and core/ExceptionUnit.v (exception handling with PC redirect to the exception vector). Test program: exp_test.s. Read the lab README and skeleton comments carefully for CSR addresses, exception causes, and the redirect interface. Verify with iverilog/vvp that normal execution and the exception path both work.

LAB 3 — directory /workspace/repo/src/lab3/. 5-stage pipeline with UART simulation support and extended control signals. Implement every TODO module: core/ALU.v, core/ImmGen.v, core/RAM_B.v (includes a simulated UART output at address 0x10000000 — check the skeleton comments for exact behavior, e.g. writing a byte there should $display/$write the character), core/Regs.v, core/REG_IF_ID.v, core/REG_ID_EX.v, core/REG_EX_MEM.v, core/REG_MEM_WB.v, common/cmp_32.v, core/CtrlUnit.v (includes CSR read/write signals and exception vector generation), core/HazardDetectionUnit.v, core/RV32core.v. The reference program is a C sort (lab3_ref/src/sort.c, compiled text in lab3_ref/obj/sort-riscv32-cpu.txt). Verify the CPU runs and produces expected output (e.g. sorted values via UART or memory).

LAB 4 — directory /workspace/repo/src/lab4/. Another 5-stage in-order pipeline variant with a different control-signal encoding, plus a cache subsystem (cache/ directory — check whether cache files are pre-provided or hollowed; implement any TODO modules there too if present). Implement every TODO module: core/ALU.v, core/ImmGen.v, core/Regs.v, core/REG_IF_ID.v, core/REG_ID_EX.v, core/REG_EX_MEM.v, core/REG_MEM_WB.v, common/cmp_32.v, core/CtrlUnit.v, core/HazardDetectionUnit.v, core/RV32core.v. Note there is no core/RAM_B.v here — data memory goes through the cache; sim/sim_top.v and sim/cmu_sim.v show how it is wired. Test program: mem_test.s. Verify with iverilog/vvp using the appropriate sim top.

LAB 5 — directory /workspace/repo/src/lab5/. Scoreboard-based out-of-order execution: IF → Issue → Read Operands → Execute (parallel functional units) → Write-Back. The scoreboard, CtrlUnit, RV32core, Regs, ImmGen, REG_IF_IS and RAM_B are PRE-PROVIDED — do not modify them. Implement ONLY the five functional units: core/FU_ALU.v (stateful ALU: latch inputs on EN, one-cycle result, full ALU op set per CtrlDefine.vh), core/FU_mul.v (multiplier FU with 64-cycle latency implemented as a shifting state register; instantiate a `multiplier` IP — if no such module exists in the repo, create a behavioral one; return the lower 32 bits), core/FU_div.v (divider FU with AXI-style valid/ready/data handshaking; instantiate a `divider` IP — create a behavioral one if missing; return the quotient from the upper 32 bits of the result bus), core/FU_jump.v (jump/branch FU: compare operands with cmp_32, target PC = (JALR ? rs1 : PC) + imm, return address = PC + 4), core/FU_mem.v (memory FU with 2-cycle latency; compute address via add_32, instantiate RAM_B for the access). Read core/CtrlDefine.vh and the pre-provided RV32core.v/scoreboard wiring to match FU port usage and done/finish handshake semantics exactly. Reference program: ref/inst.S. Verify with sim/sim_top.v via iverilog/vvp that the OoO machine writes back correct values.

LAB 6 — directory /workspace/repo/src/lab6/. Full Tomasulo out-of-order execution with reservation stations, CDB broadcast, and a RAT. Implement every TODO module: the five functional units core/FU_ALU.v, core/FU_mul.v (64-cycle shifting state register, instantiate `multiplier` IP — create a behavioral model if none exists, return lower 32 bits), core/FU_div.v (AXI handshake, instantiate `divider` IP — create if missing, quotient from upper 32 bits), core/FU_jump.v (cmp_32 compare, target = (JALR ? rs1 : PC) + imm, return PC+4), core/FU_mem.v (2-cycle latency, address via add_32, instantiate RAM_B); PLUS core/CtrlUnit.v (decode with FU routing and op encoding per core/CtrlDefine.vh), core/Regs.v (register file with Register Alias Table: implement rs_num_A/rs_num_B RAT lookups and CDB broadcast writeback), core/RAM_B.v (extended RAM with UART simulation and larger address space), core/ImmGen.v, and core/RV32core.v (top-level Tomasulo wiring: PC enable, issue enable, reservation-station allocation, RS port connections, FU port connections, CDB broadcast, stall logic). Test program: test.s / test.txt, sim testbench sim/lab6_sim.v. Read core/CtrlDefine.vh and all skeletons first; the reservation-station structure inside RV32core.v skeleton comments defines what you must wire. Verify with iverilog/vvp that the Tomasulo machine executes test.s and writes back correct values.

lastPrompt: This project implements a RISC-V (RV32IM) CPU in Verilog across six progressive undergraduate labs, each building a different microarchitectural variant. All labs share common building blocks (ALU, ImmGen, Regs, RAM, comparator, pipeline registers) but differ in pipeline organization, hazard handling, and execution model. You must implement the hollowed-out modules in every lab. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is under `/workspace/repo/src/`. Lab 1 — Basic 5-Stage In-Order Pipeline (`src/lab1/`): Classic IF → ID → EX → MEM → WB pipeline for RV32I. The ID stage resolves branches and contains forwarding muxes. Modules to implement: ALU (`core/ALU.v`): 12-operation ALU (ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, SLL, SRL, SRA, SLT, SLTU, A+4, B-passthrough) with zero and overflow flags. ImmGen (`core/ImmGen.v`): Sign-extend immediates for I/B/J/S/U formats. RAM_B (`core/RAM_B.v`): Byte-addressable data memory with byte/half/word access. Regs (`core/Regs.v`): 31-entry register file with write-through, dual read ports. REG_IF_ID (`core/REG_IF_ID.v`): IF/ID latch with stall and flush support. REG_ID_EX (`core/REG_ID_EX.v`): ID/EX latch with flush-on-hazard support. REG_EX_MEM (`core/REG_EX_MEM.v`): EX/MEM pipeline register. REG_MEM_WB (`core/REG_MEM_WB.v`): MEM/WB pipeline register. cmp_32 (`common/cmp_32.v`): 6-mode comparator (EQ, NE, LT, LTU, GE, GEU). CtrlUnit (`core/CtrlUnit.v`): Full RV32I control signal generation. HazardDetectionUnit (`core/HazardDetectionUnit.v`): Forwarding and stall logic. RV32core (`core/RV32core.v`): Top-level MUX wiring (PC select, forwarding, ALU inputs). Lab 2 — Pipeline with CSR and Exceptions (`src/lab2/`): Same 5-stage pipeline as lab1, extended with CSR registers and an exception unit. Additional modules beyond the lab1 set: CSRRegs (`core/CSRRegs.v`): CSR register file supporting CSRRW/CSRRS/CSRRC. ExceptionUnit (`core/ExceptionUnit.v`): Exception handling with PC redirect. All lab1-equivalent modules (ALU, CtrlUnit, HazardDetectionUnit, ImmGen, Regs, RAM_B, pipeline registers, RV32core) must also be implemented with CSR/exception extensions. Lab 3 — Pipeline with UART and Extended Hazards (`src/lab3/`): 5-stage pipeline with UART simulation support in RAM and extended control signals. Same module set as lab1, plus: RAM_B includes simulated UART output at address 0x10000000. CtrlUnit includes CSR read/write signals and exception vector generation. cmp_32 (`common/cmp_32.v`): Same comparator as lab1. Lab 4 — Pipeline Variant (`src/lab4/`): Another 5-stage in-order pipeline variant with a different control signal set. Same module set as lab1 (ALU, CtrlUnit, HazardDetectionUnit, ImmGen, Regs, pipeline registers, RV32core). Differences in control signal encoding. Lab 5 — Out-of-Order with Scoreboard (`src/lab5/`): Out-of-order execution using a scoreboard-based controller with dedicated functional units. Pipeline: IF → Issue → Read Operands → Execute (multiple FUs) → Write-Back. Modules to implement: FU_ALU (`core/FU_ALU.v`): Stateful ALU FU — latches inputs on EN, produces result in one cycle. Must implement state machine and full ALU computation. FU_mul (`core/FU_mul.v`): Multiplier FU with 64-cycle latency (shifting state register). Instantiate `multiplier` IP, return lower 32 bits. FU_div (`core/FU_div.v`): Divider FU using AXI handshaking (valid/ready/data). Instantiate `divider` IP, return quotient from upper 32 bits. FU_jump (`core/FU_jump.v`): Jump/branch FU — compare operands with `cmp_32`, compute target PC = (JALR ? rs1 : PC) + imm, return address = PC + 4. FU_mem (`core/FU_mem.v`): Memory FU with 2-cycle latency. Compute address via `add_32`, instantiate `RAM_B` for memory access. Lab 6 — Out-of-Order with Tomasulo/Reservation Stations (`src/lab6/`): Full Tomasulo OoO execution with reservation stations, CDB broadcast, and RAT.
